title: Comprehension: Follow the Whole Sentence
description: Practice extracting who, number, inclusion, action frame, and time clues from source-checked Hawaiian sentences.

sourceReview.notes: Source check, not educator review. Source spellings are normalized to Unicode ʻokina and NFC. Judd is not used to authorize any live form.

activities.instruction: Read for the whole message.
activities.prompt: Do not translate one word at a time.
activities.support: Use the time clue, action frame, and pronoun together.
activities.sentence: E kamaʻilio ana au iā Kimo i nehinei.
activities.naturalEnglish: I was talking to Kimo yesterday.
activities.patternIntro: The e ... ana action frame is interpreted with the past-time clue nehinei, while au identifies the speaker as the person doing the action.

parts.label: Action frame
parts.note: talking / ongoing action in this context

activities.languageNote: The reference grammar explicitly uses this example to show that e ... ana relies on surrounding context for time interpretation.

sourceRefs.section: Interrogative; A Me; Incomplete Action; Personal pronouns

activities.instruction: Understand the participant.
activities.prompt: E kamaʻilio ana au iā Kimo i nehinei.
activities.support: Who was talking?
activities.explanation: au means I, so the speaker is the person talking.

sourceRefs.section: Interrogative; A Me; Incomplete Action; Personal pronouns

activities.instruction: Use the context clue.

activities.support: Which word gives the past-time context?
activities.explanation: I nehinei means yesterday, which anchors the ongoing action in past context.

activities.instruction: Read the question as a whole.
activities.prompt: Track both the question and who is being addressed.
activities.support: The pronoun changes how many listeners are included.
activities.patternIntro: aha asks what, while ʻoe tells you the question is addressed to one person.

parts.label: Question
parts.note: what are you doing? in this sourced pattern

activities.languageNote: Recognizing ʻoe tells you the question is directed to one listener.

activities.instruction: Track the audience.
activities.support: How many people is the speaker addressing?
activities.explanation: ʻoe is second-person singular.

activities.instruction: Follow multiple participants.
activities.prompt: Notice that one sentence can contain a subject and two possessed family relationships.
activities.support: Track who is present and whose relationships are being described.
activities.sentence: Aia ʻo ia me kona makuahine a me kona makua kāne.
activities.naturalEnglish: She is with her mother and her father.
activities.patternIntro: The sentence has ʻo ia as the person located with two family members, both linked through kona.

parts.label: Relationships
parts.hawaiian: kona makuahine a me kona makua kāne

activities.languageNote: Understanding the sentence requires tracking that kona connects both family relationships to ʻo ia.

sourceRefs.section: Interrogative; A Me; Incomplete Action; Personal pronouns

activities.instruction: Track inclusion.
activities.prompt: Aia ʻo ia me kona makuahine a me kona makua kāne.
activities.support: Whose mother and father are being described?
activities.explanation: kona is third-person singular possessive in both relationships.

sourceRefs.section: Interrogative; A Me; Incomplete Action; Personal pronouns

activities.instruction: Apply the pronoun system in a new sentence.
activities.prompt: Ua ʻike ʻo ia iā mākou i ke kula.
activities.support: Who did he or she see?
options: The speaker's group of three or more, excluding the listener
activities.answer: The speaker's group of three or more, excluding the listener
activities.explanation: iā mākou refers to us — three or more including the speaker but excluding the listener.

sourceRefs.section: Interrogative; A Me; Incomplete Action; Personal pronouns

activities.instruction: Apply the same system after a preposition.
activities.prompt: E hele au me ʻoukou i ke kula.
activities.support: Who will the speaker go with?
options: You all — three or more people
activities.answer: You all — three or more people
activities.explanation: me ʻoukou means with you, addressing three or more people.

sourceRefs.section: Interrogative; A Me; Incomplete Action; Personal pronouns

activities.instruction: Use context, not a one-word translation.
activities.prompt: E kamaʻilio ana au iā Kimo i nehinei.
activities.support: Why is a past-time meaning appropriate here even though the sentence uses e ... ana?
options: Because nehinei gives a past-time context
Because au always means past tense
Because e ... ana always means past
activities.answer: Because nehinei gives a past-time context
activities.explanation: The reference grammar notes that e ... ana can describe incomplete action in different time frames; surrounding context such as nehinei determines the interpretation.
